I wrote `{"invariant_exists": false}` to the answer file: `len(equal_vars) == len(equals)` does not hold at line 139.

I got this from the recorded trace data in `question.json`. I didn't read the test cases or `cfnlint/conditions/conditions.py`, and I couldn't run anything. Each sample pair there is (`len(equal_vars)`, `len(equals)`) at line 139: (1,0), (2,1), (3,2) and so on. So at that point `equal_vars` always has one more entry than `equals`.

That fits the code order the question describes: the new entry goes into `equal_vars` first, at line 124, 126 or 128. The line-139 event fires just before `equals[c_equal.hash] = c_equal` adds the matching entry, so the two sizes differ at every sampled event. The invariant that holds there is `len(equal_vars) == len(equals) + 1`, not equality.
